extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, third‑party requesters, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners handling inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and form requirements, deadlines, and examiner treatment rules for filings, responses, service, defective papers, and appeals in inter partes reexamination under the MPEP and applicable CFR/USC provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of documents (37 CFR 1.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for inter partes reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in § 1.248. Any document must reflect service or the document may be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to serve documents may result in refusal of consideration. Service must be on all parties including other third party requesters made part of the proceeding by merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service required
rubrics_metrics.description: As proof of service, the party submitting the paper to the Office must attach a certificate of service to the paper. It is required that the certificate of service set forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the certificate of service must be attached with the copy of the paper that is served on the other party. If service was not possible, a duplicate copy of the request must be supplied to the Office. PTOL-2071 should be used as the cover sheet for mailing the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party comment deadline (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party requester must file written comments within a period of 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s response to be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proof of service is not attached, the Office will mail a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-2069) giving one month or 30 days (whichever is longer) to complete via a supplemental paper indicating the manner and date of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of defective service — timing to cure (form paragraph 26.68)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission was not served as required, the submission is defective and service and a certificate of service must be provided to the Office within ONE MONTH from the date of the letter or within the time remaining in the response period of the last Office action (whichever is longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.68 may be used to notify the submitting party (insert 'patent owner' or 'third party requester' in bracket).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeming date of service when recipient received late (>5 business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner’s response served on a third party requester is received by that requester more than 5 business days after the date of service set forth on the certificate of service, the third party requester may submit a verified statement specifying the date of actual receipt as an attachment to its comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will then deem the date of service to be the date of actual receipt by the third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of untimely/inappropriate third‑party papers (37 CFR 1.957)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the third party requester files an untimely or inappropriate comment, notice of appeal or brief in an inter partes reexamination, the paper will be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal applies to the specific submission; the third party does not necessarily lose rights to comment on future patent owner responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of patent owner failure to file timely/appropriate response (37 CFR 1.957(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If no claims are found patentable and the patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response, prosecution will be terminated and the Director will issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination (NIRC). If claims are found patentable and the patent owner fails to respond timely, further prosecution will be limited to claims found patentable at the time and to claims added thereafter that do not expand scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner will issue an Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) indicating withdrawn/canceled claims and setting periods for response and third‑party comments under 37 CFR 1.951. See MPEP §§ 2671.02 and 2671.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Action Closing Prosecution (ACP)
rubrics_metrics.description: A response to an ACP is not required. Where the patent owner does not respond to an ACP, the Office will issue a Right of Appeal Notice in due course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consequences of 37 CFR 1.957(b) and (c) do NOT apply to the patent owner’s failure to respond to an ACP (i.e., different procedures follow such as Right of Appeal Notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to make a timely appeal after issuance of a Right of Appeal Notice, or a timely appeal is dismissed, consequences depend on whether any claim was found patentable: (A) If no claim was found patentable → NIRC issued immediately. (B) If at least one claim was found patentable and third‑party requester does not appeal → prosecution terminated and NIRC issued. (C) If at least one claim patentable and third‑party appellant continues appeal → claims limited to those found patentable at time of failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the third‑party appellant continues appeal while the patent owner fails, non‑patentable claims are withdrawn pending cancellation on issuance of NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure of third party to timely comment after patent owner response
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a third party requester does not timely file written comments on a patent owner response, any subsequent submission of comments on that response will be refused consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The failure applies only to that specific response; the third party retains rights to comment on future patent owner responses. If the original response was incomplete and later completed by the owner, the third party may file comments within 30 days from service of the supplemental/complete response, except where completion only involved payment of a fee (other than excess claims fee). See MPEP § 2666.40.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party rights on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the third party requester fails to make a timely appeal or its appeal is dismissed, the requester loses further rights as appellant. However, if the patent owner continues its appeal, the third party as respondent can file a respondent brief and may enter the appeal pursuant to 37 CFR 41.77(c) and (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the third party fails to timely appeal and no other appeal is pending, prosecution may be terminated by issuance of a NIRC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission not fully responsive to a non‑final Office action (37 CFR 1.957(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A response by the patent owner is not fully responsive where a bona fide response is filed before expiration of the permissible response period but, through oversight or inadvertence, some point necessary to a full response has been omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may (A) waive non‑serious deficiencies and act on the submission, or (B) treat the submission as incomplete and notify the patent owner to complete it within a set period (usually one month) to avoid termination or limitation of prosecution. Form paragraph 26.06 may be used when option (B) is employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option A vs Option B when response not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: Option A: Waive minor deficiencies (not serious) and act on the submission. Option B: Where the omission is a serious deficiency or insufficient time remains, notify the patent owner of the deficiency and give a new time period (usually one month) to correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option A appropriate for minor omissions; Option B appropriate where deficiency must be dealt with prior to action on the merits. If corrected under Option B, the requester has 30 days from service of the corrected/supplemental response to file comments (unless only a fee was needed).

rubrics_metrics.name: No telephone notification of omission — interviews prohibited (37 CFR 1.955)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner cannot simply be notified by telephone that an omission must be supplied within the remaining time period for response; such notification would be an interview, and interviews are prohibited in inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All notifications requiring a time period for correction must be written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent omission rule and limits on repeated notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Giving a patent owner a time period to supply an omission under 37 CFR 1.957(d) applies only to inadvertent omissions, not deliberate omissions. Once the inadvertent omission is brought to the owner’s attention, inadvertence no longer exists, so a second written notification giving another new time period is not appropriate unless a different inadvertently omitted matter arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice is authorized but not required; examiners may refuse to follow it if they conclude the patent owner is abusing it to obtain additional time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner completion of response and third‑party comments thereon
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically the patent owner has 30 days or one month (whichever is longer) to complete the response. After completion, the examiner will wait two months from the date of service of the completed response before taking up the case, since the 30‑day period for third‑party comments will have expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third party may file comments on the completed response within 30 days of service of the completed response. If the original response was incomplete only because a fee was missing, the third party may not file comments after the fee is submitted because the fee adds nothing on the merits; but if the response includes argument, third parties may comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fee completion and comment rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is a failure to pay an excess claims fee by the patent owner, the new claim package in the owner’s original response is not entered until the fee is paid. The requester cannot comment on the new claim package until the owner files a supplemental paper paying the required excess claims fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party comments may be filed within 30 days from service of the patent owner’s response or paper correcting the excess claims fee deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Defective Paper — examples of defects (PTOL‑2069)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the substance of a submission is complete, the submission can be defective (an informal submission). Example defects include: (A) The paper filed does not include proof of service; (B) The paper filed is unsigned; (C) The paper filed is signed by a person who is not of record; (D) The amendment filed by the patent owner does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); (E) The amendment filed by the patent owner does not comply with 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and/or (c)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form PTOL‑2069 to notify parties; check boxes or explain further on an attached sheet. If defects are not corrected within one month or 30 days (whichever is longer), the submission will not be entered. Patent owner may request extension under 37 CFR 1.956; third party is barred from requesting extension (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling defective submissions for both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Where both the patent owner response and third party comments are defective, a PTOL‑2069 should be completed for each party setting forth the defects; copies of both completed forms are sent to all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If defect limited to signature/claim format/obvious defect, CRU technical support staff may issue PTOL‑2069 prior to forwarding to the examiner; otherwise examiner is responsible for obtaining needed corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Notice of Defective Paper — content and comment rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are given one month or 30 days (whichever is longer) from mailing date of the notice to correct the defect. If corrected submission is directed solely to form and does not go to the merits, the other party may not comment on the correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correcting a defective amendment or paying an excess claims fee that brings claims into the proceeding, after correction the third party may comment and prior arguments become relevant. Any discussion of the merits included with the defect correction must be set forth separately and clearly identified as merits; otherwise the submission may be returned and the party given one additional opportunity to correct the defect without intermixed merits discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized/premature papers will not be considered (37 CFR 1.939)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unauthorized paper is filed by any party at any time during the inter partes reexamination proceeding it will not be considered and may be returned. Unless otherwise authorized, no paper shall be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits of the inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain correspondence may be entered but not considered, or not entered and returned/expunged. Papers already scanned into the IFW that are inappropriate will be marked 'non‑public' and 'closed' (expunged from public record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patent owner papers expunged — premature submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any response/comments or amendment by the patent owner filed prior to the first Office action is premature and will be expunged (37 CFR 1.939). Petitions requesting merger or stay filed prior to the order to reexamine will also be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the expunged paper is accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 or 1.183, the matter should be addressed in OPLA for decision on the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and 'Response Is Too Long' (37 CFR 1.943)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the length of the patent owner submission exceeds that permitted by 37 CFR 1.943, the submission is improper and may be expunged (or the owner given options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will mail a Notice permitting the owner to (A) submit a redrafted response within the page limit or (B) file a copy of the supplemental response with pages redacted to satisfy page limits. The Notice sets 15 days to respond. If no response, submission will not be considered and prosecution may be terminated or limited. Certain pages are excluded from the 1.943 page limits (table of contents, table of case law, pages of the claims (not claim charts), claims appendix, and specific brief sections limited to required information). Affidavits/declarations that include opinion/argument are counted toward page limits; factual declarations and exhibits generally are not counted unless they include argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper patent owner response post‑ACP (1.951/1.957)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner can only file once under 37 CFR 1.951(a). Any second or supplemental submission after ACP by the patent owner will be expunged unless prosecution has been reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers expunged for this reason and not accompanied by appropriate petition will be removed by CRU Director or SPRS; petitions under 1.182 or 1.183 are addressed in OPLA.
